cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.22)

#
# This file is generated only once,
# and is not re-generated if converter is called multiple times.
#
# User is free to modify the file as much as necessary
#

# Setup compiler settings
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 11)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_C_EXTENSIONS ON)
# gnu++20: matches the Nx_WebServer draft's CUBE_CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS (-std=gnu++20), needed
# for app.cpp (structured bindings, std::unique_ptr/vector usage throughout).
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS ON)


# Define the build type
if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
    set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE "Debug")
endif()

# Set the project name
set(CMAKE_PROJECT_NAME firmware_factory_control_unit)

# Enable compile command to ease indexing with e.g. clangd
set(CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS TRUE)

# Core project settings
project(${CMAKE_PROJECT_NAME})
message("Build type: " ${CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE})

# Enable CMake support for ASM, C and C++ languages
enable_language(C CXX ASM)

# Create an executable object type
add_executable(${CMAKE_PROJECT_NAME})

# Add STM32CubeMX generated sources
add_subdirectory(cmake/stm32cubemx)

# TIM6 wieder freigegeben: die .ioc-Zeitbasis wurde (ueber die CubeMX-GUI, nicht per Text-Edit --
# ein Blind-Edit dieser Einstellung erwies sich zuvor als zu fragil, mehrere verzahnte
# .ioc-Schluessel wie ein VP_SYS_VS_*-virtueller Pin haengen daran) von TIM6 auf SysTick
# umgestellt. CubeMX generiert stm32h5xx_hal_timebase_tim.c dadurch gar nicht mehr -- kein
# CMake-seitiger Ausschluss mehr noetig, TIM6 ist regenerationssicher frei. HAL_InitTick/
# HAL_GetTick/HAL_Delay/HAL_SuspendTick/HAL_ResumeTick sind trotzdem weiterhin in
# Core/Src/hal_tick_threadx.c stark neu definiert (ThreadX tx_time_get()/tx_thread_sleep(), mit
# DWT-Zykluszaehler-Fallback vor Scheduler-Start bzw. aus einer ISR heraus) -- CubeMX wuerde sonst
# nur auf den (von ThreadX exklusiv beanspruchten) SysTick zurueckfallen.

# ST's eigene PCD-Header (stm32h5xx_hal_pcd.h, PCD_GET_EP_*_CNT()-Makros) verwenden
# "count--" auf volatile-qualifizierten Structmembern -- ab GCC13/-std=c++20 dafuer ein
# "-Wvolatile"-Deprecation-Warning. Ein #pragma GCC system_header direkt in der Datei wuerde
# bei jedem CubeMX "Generate Code" wieder verschwinden (wie schon einmal geschehen); hier am
# INTERFACE-Target "stm32cubemx" (propagiert an alle Consumer, auch die stm32_libs-Unterprojekte)
# ist die Unterdrueckung stabil, weil dieses Root-CMakeLists.txt nicht von CubeMX ueberschrieben wird.
target_compile_options(stm32cubemx INTERFACE $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:-Wno-volatile>)

# STM32H5 / STM32H5xx: family macros that the shared stm32_libs (common_stm32/tmc2209/
# usb_pd, see the add_subdirectory() calls below) branch on, in addition to the
# chip-specific STM32H563xx that CubeMX's own MX_Defines_Syms already defines
# (cmake/stm32cubemx/CMakeLists.txt) -- added here instead of there since that file is
# regenerated by CubeMX on every "Generate Code" and would silently drop this again.
target_compile_definitions(stm32cubemx INTERFACE STM32H5 STM32H5xx)

# --- Test-Rig-Umschaltung: STM32H5 Nucleo-144 (NUCLEO-H563ZI, siehe UM3115) statt der echten
# Factory-Control-Unit-Platine -- fuer Bring-up/Test, wenn das eigentliche Board (noch) nicht
# verfuegbar ist. Aktivieren per "cmake --preset Debug-Nucleo" (s. CMakePresets.json) oder
# "-DBOARD_NUCLEO_H563ZI=ON". Betrifft nur die Pins, die zwischen beiden Boards tatsaechlich
# unterschiedlich verdrahtet sind (Ethernet TX_EN/TXD0, s. HAL_ETH_MspInit in
# stm32h5xx_hal_msp.c) plus zwei neue Ersatzsignale (Board-Taste B1 simuliert LIGHTBARRIER1,
# Board-LED LD1 simuliert CONVEYOR, s. main.h/main.c/io.cpp) -- USB (PA11/PA12, interner
# USB_DRD_FS-Controller ohne AF-Pinmux) ist auf beiden Boards identisch verdrahtet und braucht
# keine Unterscheidung. Alle uebrigen Modbus-Funktionen (Stepper/Ventile/ToF/EtherCAT/...)
# bleiben unveraendert im Code, laufen auf dem Nucleo aber ins Leere (Pins dort unbeschaltet) --
# laut Anforderung muessen sie dort nicht funktionieren, duerfen den Boot aber auch nicht
# aufhalten (bereits so gebaut: keine der Setup()-Routinen dieser Subsysteme haengt sich an
# einem Error_Handler() auf, s. Kommentar bei tof_color_.Setup() in io.cpp).
option(BOARD_NUCLEO_H563ZI "Build for the STM32H563ZI Nucleo-144 eval board (UM3115) instead of the real Factory Control Unit PCB" OFF)
if(BOARD_NUCLEO_H563ZI)
    message(STATUS "Board target: STM32H563ZI Nucleo-144 (test rig)")
    target_compile_definitions(stm32cubemx INTERFACE BOARD_NUCLEO_H563ZI)
else()
    message(STATUS "Board target: Factory Control Unit (real PCB)")
endif()

# Link directories setup
target_link_directories(${CMAKE_PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE
    # Add user defined library search paths
)

# --- opcua_native: from-scratch OPC UA Binary server (modern C++, no external OPC UA
# dependency) -- see libs/opcua_native/ for the design. Built up in layers, each independently
# buildable as this object library grows: types/byte_stream (header-only) + codec/variant
# (pure C++, no hardware headers) today; transport/session/services/address-space +
# NetX Duo/ThreadX wiring get added (and their own include dirs/defines, mirroring the
# open62541 port's approach on the sibling branch) as they're written.
add_library(opcua_native OBJECT
    libs/opcua_native/src/codec.cpp
    libs/opcua_native/src/variant.cpp
    libs/opcua_native/src/tcp_message.cpp
    libs/opcua_native/src/service_header.cpp
    libs/opcua_native/src/clock.cpp
    libs/opcua_native/src/secure_channel.cpp
    libs/opcua_native/src/service_structs.cpp
    libs/opcua_native/src/session.cpp
    libs/opcua_native/src/services.cpp
    libs/opcua_native/src/connection.cpp
    libs/opcua_native/src/net_transport.cpp
)
target_include_directories(opcua_native PUBLIC
    libs/opcua_native/include
)
# net_transport.cpp/.hpp need NX_TCPSERVER (nx_tcpserver.h) + ThreadX headers -- everything
# else in this target is pure portable C++ (no hardware/RTOS headers).
#
# Compile definitions MUST match the main firmware target's exactly (not just tx_time_get()-
# relevant ones): nx_tcpserver.c itself is only ever compiled ONCE, as part of
# ${CMAKE_PROJECT_NAME} using ITS defines (notably NX_WEB_HTTPS_ENABLE, which adds a TLS
# session field to NX_TCP_SESSION and changes sizeof(NX_TCP_SESSION)) -- net_transport.hpp
# declares an NX_TCP_SESSION array itself (OpcUaTcpServer::sessions_), so a mismatched view of
# that struct's size here would corrupt memory silently (session-array indexing would disagree
# with what nx_tcpserver.c itself computes internally). See the open62541 branch's identical
# note for the full reasoning -- same lesson, independently rediscovered while porting this
# transport layer.
target_include_directories(opcua_native PRIVATE
    libs/ST/threadx/common/inc
    libs/ST/threadx/ports/cortex_m33/gnu/inc
    libs/ST/netxduo/common/inc
    libs/ST/netxduo/ports/cortex_m33/gnu/inc
    libs/ST/netxduo/addons/web
    libs/ST/netxduo/nx_secure/inc
    libs/ST/netxduo/nx_secure/ports
    libs/ST/netxduo/crypto_libraries/inc
    libs/ST/netxduo/crypto_libraries/ports/cortex_m4/gnu/inc
)
target_compile_definitions(opcua_native PRIVATE
    FX_INCLUDE_USER_DEFINE_FILE
    NX_INCLUDE_USER_DEFINE_FILE
    TX_INCLUDE_USER_DEFINE_FILE
    UX_INCLUDE_USER_DEFINE_FILE
    TX_SINGLE_MODE_NON_SECURE=1
    NX_SECURE_INCLUDE_USER_DEFINE_FILE
    NX_WEB_HTTPS_ENABLE
    NX_SECURE_ENABLE_ECC_CIPHERSUITE
    NX_SECURE_ENABLE_AEAD_CIPHER
)
target_link_libraries(opcua_native PRIVATE stm32cubemx)

# ThreadX/FileX/NetXDuo (vendored under libs/ST/{threadx,filex,netxduo}, renamed from
# "Middlewares" to "libs" so STM32CubeMX's regeneration doesn't treat/delete it as its
# own middleware output -- see Nx_WebServer, the draft this was transferred from, for
# the original layout). Explicit per-component GLOBs instead of one recursive glob over
# all of libs/ST: each package ships several port/toolchain variants and only the
# cortex_m33/gnu ones (already the only ones vendored here) should be compiled.
file(GLOB THREADX_SOURCES
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/ST/threadx/common/src/*.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/ST/threadx/ports/cortex_m33/gnu/src/*.S
)
file(GLOB FILEX_SOURCES
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/ST/filex/common/src/*.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/ST/filex/common/drivers/*.c
)
file(GLOB NETXDUO_SOURCES
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/ST/netxduo/common/src/*.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/ST/netxduo/common/drivers/ethernet/*.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/ST/netxduo/common/drivers/ethernet/lan8742/*.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/ST/netxduo/addons/dhcp/*.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/ST/netxduo/addons/mdns/*.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/ST/netxduo/addons/web/*.c
)
# NetX Secure (TLS) + Crypto -- wegen der Dateimenge (~360 Dateien) per GLOB statt
# Hand-Liste eingebunden (identisches Muster wie in Nx_WebServer/CMakeLists.txt).
file(GLOB_RECURSE NX_SECURE_SOURCES
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/ST/netxduo/nx_secure/src/*.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/ST/netxduo/crypto_libraries/src/*.c
)

# USBX (vendort aus STMicroelectronics/stm32-mw-usbx, ST's Fork von eclipse-threadx/usbx --
# upstream fehlt der STM32-Geraetetreiber usbx_stm32_device_controllers komplett). Nur
# Device-Seite (kein usbx_host_classes/usbx_host_controllers/ux_hcd_sim_host/ux_dcd_sim_slave/
# dpump-Demoklasse -- dieses Geraet ist nie USB-Host, s. UX_DEVICE_SIDE_ONLY in ux_user.h) und
# nur die eine tatsaechlich genutzte ST-eigene Geraeteklasse (cdc_acm) statt aller
# usbx_device_classes/* (analog zur Kuration bei tinyusb_port/den NetX-Duo-Addons oben) --
# urspruenglich cdc_ecm (kein Windows-Treiber verfuegbar), danach rndis (Windows-Bluescreen,
# s. Commit-Historie), beide inzwischen entfernt. Das Netzwerk-Interface ist seitdem eine
# komplett projekteigene CDC-NCM-Klasse (Core/Src/usbd_ncm.c, s. dortiger Klassenkommentar), die
# sich aber -- genau wie es cdc_ecm/rndis taten -- ueber USBX' eigenen generischen
# NetX-Duo-Bruecken-Treiber (_ux_network_driver_entry/_activate/_deactivate/_link_up/_down/
# _packet_received) an NetX Duo anbindet, statt einen eigenen Treiber mitzubringen -- deshalb
# bleibt usbx_network/src im GLOB, es wird weiterhin aktiv gebraucht.
file(GLOB USBX_SOURCES
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/ST/usbx/common/core/src/*.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/ST/usbx/common/usbx_device_classes/src/*.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/ST/usbx/common/usbx_network/src/*.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/ST/usbx/common/usbx_stm32_device_controllers/*.c
)
# ux_system_tasks_run.c ist der Task-Runner fuer den "Standalone"-Modus (kooperatives Polling
# ohne RTOS-Threads, s. UX_STANDALONE in ux_user.h) und braucht dafuer bedingungslos
# ux_host_stack.h -- das Projekt nutzt aber den regulaeren Thread-Modus (UX_STANDALONE
# undefiniert), und die Host-Stack-Sourcen/Header wurden gar nicht erst vendort (Device-only,
# s. Kommentar oben). Datei ist damit fuer dieses Projekt totes Gewicht und muss raus, sonst
# bricht der Build am fehlenden Header ab.
list(FILTER USBX_SOURCES EXCLUDE REGEX "ux_system_tasks_run\\.c$")

# --- Binaer-Assets (Geraetezertifikat/-schluessel + komprimierte Weboberflaeche) ---
# Statt wie frueher generierter C-Arrays (Core/Src/generated/device_certificate.c,
# modbus_ui_page.c, beide eingecheckt) werden jetzt die rohen Binaerdateien selbst verwendet
# (build/assets/*.der von den Phasen ReadHardwareIds + GenerateCertificates... + GenerateDeviceArtifacts/
# CopyGeneratedFilesToBuildDirectory, build/assets/index.html.br von der Phase BuildWebApp --
# s. builder/, docs/build-process.md) und bei jedem Build per objcopy zu je
# einem .o konvertiert -- landen in der eigenen .flash_assets-Linker-Section (s.
# STM32H563xx_FLASH.ld), objcopy liefert dazu automatisch die Symbole
# _binary_<sanitierter-Dateiname>_start/_end (Laenge per Zeigerdifferenz, s. net_setup.cpp/
# webserver.cpp). build/assets/ liegt bewusst unter build/ (nicht als eigener Top-Level-Ordner):
# beide sind vollstaendig generierte, gitignorte Snapshots aus dem Board-Archiv bzw. Web-Build,
# genau wie build/.last-board-id -- unabhaengig vom jeweiligen CMake-Preset, deshalb
# CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR (Repo-Wurzel) statt CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR (preset-spezifisch,
# ${sourceDir}/build/<preset>/), sonst gaebe es pro Preset eine eigene Kopie von Zertifikat/
# Schluessel/Web-Bundle statt einer gemeinsamen.
set(BINARY_ASSETS
    "build/assets/device_certificate.der"
    "build/assets/device_key.der"
    "build/assets/index.html.br"
)

set(ASSET_H_FILE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/generated/assets.h")
set(ASSET_H_CONTENT "// Automatisch generierte Asset-Deklarationen aus BINARY_ASSETS (s. CMakeLists.txt).\n// Nicht manuell bearbeiten!\n#pragma once\n\n#include <stdint.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n")

set(ASSET_OBJ_FILES "")
foreach(BIN_FILE_PATH ${BINARY_ASSETS})
    get_filename_component(BIN_NAME ${BIN_FILE_PATH} NAME)
    set(OBJ_FILE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/assets/${BIN_NAME}.o")
    list(APPEND ASSET_OBJ_FILES ${OBJ_FILE})

    string(MAKE_C_IDENTIFIER ${BIN_NAME} C_NAME)
    set(SYM_START "_binary_${C_NAME}_start")
    set(SYM_END "_binary_${C_NAME}_end")

    # objcopy backt bei "-I binary" den kompletten (relativen) Eingabepfad in den Symbolnamen
    # ein, nicht nur den Dateinamen -- WORKING_DIRECTORY sorgt dafuer, dass nur der blanke
    # Dateiname ("build/assets/device_certificate.der" -> "device_certificate.der") einfliesst,
    # damit SYM_START/SYM_END unten tatsaechlich zu den erzeugten Symbolen passen.
    add_custom_command(
        OUTPUT ${OBJ_FILE}
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E make_directory "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/assets"
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_OBJCOPY} -I binary -O elf32-littlearm --rename-section .data=.flash_assets
                "${BIN_NAME}" "${OBJ_FILE}"
        WORKING_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/build/assets"
        DEPENDS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/${BIN_FILE_PATH}"
        COMMENT "Konvertiere ${BIN_NAME} zu Flash-Asset-Objekt..."
        VERBATIM
    )

    string(APPEND ASSET_H_CONTENT "extern const uint8_t ${SYM_START}[];\nextern const uint8_t ${SYM_END}[];\n")
endforeach()

string(APPEND ASSET_H_CONTENT "\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n")

file(MAKE_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/generated")
file(WRITE ${ASSET_H_FILE} "${ASSET_H_CONTENT}")

    libs/hw/vl53l0x/vl53l0x.cpp
    libs/hw/tcs34725/tcs34725.cpp
    libs/hw/ina226/ina226.cpp
    Drivers/BSP/Components/lan8742/lan8742.c
    ${ASSET_OBJ_FILES}
    ${THREADX_SOURCES}

    ${NETXDUO_SOURCES}
    ${NX_SECURE_SOURCES}
    ${USBX_SOURCES}
)

# Add include paths
target_include_directories(${CMAKE_PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE

    # "Core" (zusaetzlich zu "Core/Src") loest "#include \"generated/*.hh\"" gegen

    # bleiben dadurch unveraendert, nur der von builder/ CopyGeneratedFilesToBuildDirectory

    Core
    Core/Src
    libs/ST/threadx/common/inc
    libs/ST/threadx/ports/cortex_m33/gnu/inc
    libs/ST/filex/common/inc
    libs/ST/filex/common/drivers
    libs/ST/filex/ports/generic/inc
    libs/ST/netxduo/common/inc
    libs/ST/netxduo/ports/cortex_m33/gnu/inc
    libs/ST/netxduo/common/drivers/ethernet
    libs/ST/netxduo/common/drivers/ethernet/lan8742
    libs/ST/netxduo/addons/dhcp
    libs/ST/netxduo/addons/mdns
    libs/ST/netxduo/addons/web
    libs/ST/netxduo/nx_secure/inc
    libs/ST/netxduo/nx_secure/ports
    libs/ST/netxduo/crypto_libraries/inc
    libs/ST/netxduo/crypto_libraries/ports/cortex_m4/gnu/inc
    libs/ST/usbx/common/core/inc
    libs/ST/usbx/common/usbx_device_classes/inc
    libs/ST/usbx/common/usbx_network/inc
    libs/ST/usbx/common/usbx_stm32_device_controllers
    libs/ST/usbx/ports/generic/inc
    Drivers/BSP/Components/lan8742
    # Header-only stm32_libs (kein eigenes CMake-Target, kein add_subdirectory noetig) --
    # gpio.hh/log.h/hal_header_selector.h etc. kommen bereits transitiv ueber das Linken gegen

    ../stm32_libs/hx711

    libs/hw/vl53l0x
    libs/hw/tcs34725
    libs/hw/ws2812
    libs/hw/ina226
    # generated/assets.h -- s. ASSET_H_FILE/BINARY_ASSETS oben (CMake-eigene Objcopy-Mechanik,
    # keine "Codegenerierung" im Sinne von builder/, s. docs/build-process.md Abschnitt 11).
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/generated
)

# Add project symbols (macros)
target_compile_definitions(${CMAKE_PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE
    # Add user defined symbols
    # *_INCLUDE_USER_DEFINE_FILE: pulls in Core/Inc/{tx,nx,fx}_user.h (pool sizes/tick
    # rate/etc.), without these ThreadX/NetXDuo/FileX silently fall back to their
    # built-in defaults instead.
    FX_INCLUDE_USER_DEFINE_FILE
    NX_INCLUDE_USER_DEFINE_FILE
    TX_INCLUDE_USER_DEFINE_FILE
    UX_INCLUDE_USER_DEFINE_FILE
    # TrustZone: this core runs the CORTEX_M33_NS (non-secure) image only, no
    # Secure/Non-secure ThreadX handoff -- matches Nx_WebServer's build (STM32H573I-DK
    # is TrustZone-disabled there for the same reason).
    TX_SINGLE_MODE_NON_SECURE=1
    NX_SECURE_INCLUDE_USER_DEFINE_FILE
    NX_WEB_HTTPS_ENABLE
    NX_SECURE_ENABLE_ECC_CIPHERSUITE
    NX_SECURE_ENABLE_AEAD_CIPHER
)

# -fno-use-cxa-atexit: avoids pulling in __cxa_atexit/__dso_handle for global C++
# destructor registration (never runs on this target, matches Nx_WebServer's CXX flags).
target_compile_options(${CMAKE_PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE
    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:-fno-use-cxa-atexit>
)

# Remove wrong libob.a library dependency when using cpp files
list(REMOVE_ITEM CMAKE_C_IMPLICIT_LINK_LIBRARIES ob)

# --- stm32_libs (common_stm32/tmc2209/usb_pd) integration ---
# Out-of-tree add_subdirectory() needs an explicit binary dir. These libraries link
# PUBLIC against a target named "stm32cubemx" for their HAL/CMSIS include dirs and
# compile flags/defines -- already provided as an INTERFACE target by
# cmake/stm32cubemx/CMakeLists.txt (extended with STM32H5/STM32H5xx above).
add_subdirectory(../stm32_libs/common_stm32 ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/stm32_libs/common_stm32)
add_subdirectory(../stm32_libs/tmc2209 ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/stm32_libs/tmc2209)
add_subdirectory(../stm32_libs/usb_pd ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/stm32_libs/usb_pd)
# USBX (anders als TinyUSB) wird nicht als eigenes stm32_libs-Wrapper-Target eingebunden,
# sondern direkt als GLOB in target_sources()/target_include_directories() oben, analog zu
# ThreadX/FileX/NetX Duo -- s. USBX_SOURCES-Kommentar weiter oben zur Begruendung.

# Add linked libraries
target_link_libraries(${CMAKE_PROJECT_NAME}
    stm32cubemx
    common_stm32
    tmc2209
    usb_pd
    opcua_native

    # Add user defined libraries
)
